_comment: EXAMPLE MISSION -- edit this file to define YOUR route order.
This encodes the sequence you described: mud course -> U-turn -> slopes
-> avoid compost pit -> gravel -> cement -> choose court or pathway.
Each stage = behaviour + exit test + guards. Behaviours:
follow      : camera-guided open-surface following (the normal mode)
pivot_left  : turn in place left  (open-loop, timed)
pivot_right : turn in place right (open-loop, timed)
creep       : follow, but slowly (for steps, ramps, gravel)
straight    : ignore steering, drive straight (short bursts only)
Exit tests (first one that fires wins; timeout_s is the safety net):
landmark: name registered in the LandmarkBook
keepout_bias: constant steer offset (+right/-left). Use when a hazard is
always on one known side, e.g. grass embankment always on the right.

stages.name: mud_course
stages.notes: Drive the length of the mud court. Grass embankment is on the RIGHT (see Photos/IMG20260728121844.jpg) so bias gently LEFT. The court itself has ~30% grass tufts - that is drivable, not a keep-out.

stages.name: u_turn
stages.notes: OPEN-LOOP timed pivot - drifts a few degrees per run. Add an MPU-6050 IMU to make this closed-loop and repeatable.

stages.name: slopes
stages.notes: Sloped/embankment section. Higher speed = more torque for the climb; creep behaviour keeps steering gentle so the car does not slew sideways across the slope.

stages.name: avoid_compost_pit
stages.notes: The compost pit is an EXCAVATED HOLE (Photos/IMG20260728133107.jpg) - a negative obstacle the ultrasonic sensor CANNOT see. It is flanked by bright-green sacks. Bias right, and use the green_sack marker to confirm we are alongside it.

stages.name: gravel_crossing
stages.notes: Loose gravel - low traction, wheels sink. Slow + high torque. Surface reads ~0.87 hard / low saturation.

stages.name: cement_run
stages.notes: On the cement apron/pathway. Final stage - choose the pathway rather than the court by biasing away from the court edge, or split this into two stages with a marker to pick the branch.
